items.title: A closure-typed selector subject (`(impl List<\|T\| i32>)`) never selects its block, even with a bare name - unification of the closure type against the block's subject fails
items.discussion: lane lang-56b (Order 56): A181 made root-headed subjects resolve in every type position including closure types, and found that a closure-typed subject admitted nothing BEFORE the change too: the selector's subject-vs-block-subject unification does not match function types
items.body: The selector matcher compares a written subject against each block's subject by unification; a closure type (`|T| i32`, `(|| View) context owner_scope`) is apparently not unified structurally (parameters, result, the context clause), so no block with such a subject is ever admitted - a `import m::(impl \|T\| i32);` admits nothing and row 496's 'admits nothing' message fires, which at least is honest. Rec: unify function types structurally in the selector matcher (arity, each parameter, the result, `sync`/`async`/context markers as the block's spelling has them), pin bare and absolute forms. Sizing S.

items.title: `module_resolution::b576` fails in the FULL binary under plain `cargo test` (the base cache shows 0 hits) and passes alone and under nextest - base-cache sharing between threads of one process is the likely cause
items.discussion: lane lang-56b (Order 56): seen on the A182 tree (`cargo test -p vilan-core --test module_resolution` exit 101, b576 alone green, nextest's process-per-test green); not confirmed to be pre-existing but nothing in A181/A182 touches the base cache
items.body: Probably the same family as N189 (SWITCH_LOCK) and the earlier per-process world tests: b576 counts base-cache hits, and another thread's analysis in the same process either evicts or pre-fills the cache so the count reads 0. Rec: confirm on next alone; if it reproduces, make the counter per-test (the census already names the program) or mark the binary nextest-only in the same note N189 writes. Sizing S.
